q: Give one word for the following. The study of pre-historic people and their cultures
explanation:
Archaeology studies past (especially pre-historic) human life and cultures through excavated remains (tools, pottery, bones). History relies on written records; neurology is the study of the nervous system.
Memory hook: archae- = ancient (as in 'archaic') + -logy = study -> 'study of the ancient'.

q: Give one word for the following. One who is outgoing and outspoken
explanation:
An extrovert is sociable, outgoing and expressive. Its opposite, an introvert, is reserved and inward-looking. 'Friendly' is a general adjective, not the one-word term for this personality type.
Memory hook: extro- = outward (like 'exit'), intro- = inward (like 'into').

q: Give one word for the following. Equally skillful with each hand
explanation:
Ambidextrous = able to use the right and left hands equally well. (Luscious = richly delicious; misanthrope = one who hates mankind.)
Memory hook: ambi- = both (ambivalent, ambiguous) + dexter = right hand -> 'both hands are right hands'.

q: Give one word for the following. A person who teaches dance moves
explanation:
A choreographer designs and teaches the sequence of dance movements. A dancer performs them.
Memory hook: 'chorea' = dance (Greek; also the St. Vitus' dance disease) + -grapher = writer -> 'one who writes the dance'.

q: Give one word for the following. An imaginary ideal society free of poverty and suffering
explanation:
Utopia (from Thomas More's 1516 book) is an imagined perfect society. Its opposite is dystopia. Paradise/Eden are religious ideas of a heavenly garden; Arcadia is an idealised rural paradise, not a society free of poverty.
Memory hook: Greek ou-topos = 'no place' -- a perfect society that exists nowhere.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate word: That has got to be the ___ game I have ever seen
explanation:
'The ... I have ever seen' compares one thing with all others, so the superlative is needed: bad -> worse (comparative, two things) -> worst (superlative, three or more). 'Worsted' is a type of wool yarn; 'worsed' is not a word.
Memory hook: 'the + -est/-st + ever' = superlative -> the worst ever.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate word: The young man was as ___ as a peacock on buying his first car.
explanation:
Fixed simile: 'as proud as a peacock' -- the peacock displays its tail feathers as if showing off.
Memory hook: the peacock 'P'-rides itself -> Proud as a Peacock (P-P alliteration).

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate word: In the past, a feast was an ___ for informal trade.
explanation:
'Occasion for' = an event or opportunity that allows something to happen. An 'incident' is an unplanned (often unpleasant) happening; 'impulse' is a sudden urge; 'agreement' does not fit 'an ___ for trade' here.
Memory hook: a feast is an occasion (festive event) -- occasions give opportunities.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate word: I put my phone ___ silent mode when I entered the Doctor's chamber.
explanation:
Devices are set 'on' a setting: on silent, on vibrate, on mute, on speaker. 'Put your phone on silent' is the standard idiom, so 'on' is the most likely key.
Memory hook: think of a switch -- a device is ON a setting (on silent, on hold, on speaker).
note: Once the word 'mode' is added, 'in silent mode' is at least as common and fully standard ('The phone is in silent mode'), so option c 'In' is equally defensible. 'On' is the most likely official key because the bare idiom is 'on silent'. Source: https://forum.wordreference.com/threads/in-on-silent-mode.2087620/

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate word: The arrested thief was as ___ as a cucumber
explanation:
Fixed simile: 'as cool as a cucumber' = very calm and composed, even under pressure (the inside of a cucumber stays cooler than the air).
Memory hook: cucumber slices are put on eyes to 'cool' them -> cool as a cucumber.
note: Option b is printed as 'Gluity' in the original; corrected to 'Guilty'.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate and suitable word: I don't think these plants are ___ to Meghalaya.
explanation:
Indigenous = native to a place (indigenous to Meghalaya). Ingenuous = innocent, naive, frank. Ingenious = clever, inventive. 'Indogenic' is not a standard word.
Memory hook: INDIGENous -> 'born IN the region' (gen = birth); inGENIUS -> genius = clever; ingenUOUS -> naive, 'U are too trusting'.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate and suitable word: I just wanted to ___ you for the wonderful speech you gave tonight.
explanation:
Compliment (with i) = praise. Complement (with e) = something that completes or goes well with another (the wine complements the meal).
Memory hook: 'I like to give compliments' (i = I praise); complEment completes (e for 'enough / complete').

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate and suitable word: A paperback ___ of the book was released yesterday.
explanation:
Edition = a particular version or printing of a book (paperback edition, hardcover edition). Addition = something added (+). Editorial = an opinion article by the editor.
Memory hook: EDITion comes from the EDITor/publisher; ADDition = ADD.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate and suitable word: There was no one else in the room ___ for Jim.
explanation:
'Except for' = excluding / apart from. Accept = to receive or agree to. Expect = to anticipate. 'Exception' is a noun and cannot take this slot.
Memory hook: EXcept = EXclude (both start with 'ex'); ACcept = ACknowledge/receive.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate and suitable word: The ___ of the medicine on her illness was surprisingly fast
explanation:
After 'the ... of', a noun is needed. Effect (noun) = result. Affect is normally a verb = to influence. 'Impact' is also a noun, but the idiomatic collocation is 'the effect of a medicine on ...' and this set is testing affect/effect.
Memory hook: RAVEN -- Remember: Affect = Verb, Effect = Noun. (The medicine affects you; the effect is fast.)
note: 'Impact' (c) is also a noun and 'The impact of the medicine on her illness was surprisingly fast' is grammatical and meaningful, so two options are defensible. 'Effect' is the intended answer (the affect/effect pair is being tested and 'the effect of X on Y' is the standard collocation).

q: Complete the phrase: A blessing in ___
explanation:
'A blessing in disguise' = something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good.
Memory hook: the blessing is wearing a disguise (costume) of bad luck.

q: Complete the phrase: Beat around the ___
explanation:
'Beat around (about) the bush' = avoid coming to the main point. (Hunters beat bushes to drive birds out instead of going straight for them.)
Memory hook: stop beating the bush -- get to the bird (the point).

q: Complete the phrase: A stitch in time saves ___
explanation:
'A stitch in time saves nine' = fixing a small problem early prevents it becoming a bigger one (one stitch now saves nine stitches later).
Memory hook: 'time' rhymes with 'nine'.

q: Complete the phrase: We'll cross that ___ when we come to it
explanation:
'Cross that bridge when we come to it' = deal with a problem only when it actually arises, not worry in advance.
Memory hook: you can only cross a bridge when you reach it.

q: Complete the phrase: Birds of a feather flock ___
explanation:
'Birds of a feather flock together' = people with similar interests or character tend to associate with each other.
Memory hook: a flock is by definition together.

q: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: At the drop of a hat
explanation:
'At the drop of a hat' = immediately, without hesitation (from races/fights that started when a hat was dropped as the signal).
Memory hook: the hat drops -> you go instantly.

q: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Under the weather
explanation:
'Under the weather' = feeling slightly ill or unwell (sea-sick sailors were sent below deck, away from the weather).
Memory hook: when you're sick you feel 'below' your usual self.

q: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Tie the knot
explanation:
'Tie the knot' = to get married (from hand-fasting ceremonies where the couple's hands were tied together).
Memory hook: two people are 'knotted' together for life.

q: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Cut corners
options: When something is done badly to save money
explanation:
'Cut corners' = do something in the cheapest or quickest way, sacrificing quality or ignoring rules.
Memory hook: cutting across a corner is a shortcut -- shortcuts compromise quality.

q: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase: Zero tolerance
options: No credit given for work badly done
Severest punishment possible for committing a crime
explanation:
'Zero tolerance' = a policy of not tolerating any wrongdoing at all, strictly punishing even minor offences. Of the options, 'severest punishment possible for committing a crime' is the closest.
Memory hook: tolerance = 0 -> no leniency, full punishment.
note: The exact meaning is 'no tolerance of any rule-breaking (strict enforcement)'; option c is the nearest printed choice.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: Adversity
explanation:
Adversity = hardship, misfortune. Opposite = prosperity (good fortune, success). Calamity is a synonym (disaster).
Memory hook: adverse = against you; prosperity = things go 'pro' (for) you.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: Barren
explanation:
Barren = unable to produce crops/offspring. Opposite = fertile. Sterile is a synonym (trap option).
Memory hook: barren land is bare; fertile land is full.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: Capable
explanation:
Capable = having the ability to do something. Opposite = incompetent (lacking ability).
Memory hook: capable = can; incompetent = can't.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: Haughty
explanation:
Haughty = arrogantly proud. Opposite = humble (modest). Arrogant is a synonym (trap).
Memory hook: haughty holds the head 'high' (haut = high in French); humble stays low.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word: Admit
explanation:
Admit = confess / accept as true. Opposite = deny. (Admit in the sense 'let in' has 'allow' as a synonym -- trap.)
Memory hook: the accused either admits or denies the charge.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate preposition: The store I was telling you about is ___ the street.
explanation:
'Across the street' = on the opposite side of the street.
Memory hook: you walk ACROSS a street to reach the other side.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate preposition: She is scared to go out ___ night.
explanation:
Time prepositions: AT night, at noon, at 5 o'clock; IN the morning/evening; ON a day/date (on Monday).
Memory hook: 'in the morning, in the evening, but AT night'.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate preposition: We have been living ___ Chandigarh for the past eight years.
explanation:
Use IN for cities, states and countries (live in Chandigarh); AT for specific points/addresses (at the station, at 12 Park Street).
Memory hook: big area = IN, exact point = AT.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate preposition: My cousins arrived here yesterday ___ Chennai.
explanation:
'From' marks the starting point of movement: arrived from Chennai. 'By' is used for the means of transport (by train).
Memory hook: FROM = origin, TO = destination.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate preposition: We travelled by boat ___ get to the island.
explanation:
Before a base verb ('get'), purpose is expressed with the infinitive marker 'to' (= in order to): travelled by boat to get to the island.
Memory hook: why did we travel? TO get there -- 'to + verb' = purpose.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article: They usually spend their holidays in ___ hills.
explanation:
'The hills' / 'the mountains' / 'the seaside' refers to hilly regions in general as a known holiday destination, and ranges of hills/mountains take 'the'. 'A/An' cannot go with a plural noun.
Memory hook: plural + specific type of place -> THE (the hills, the Himalayas).

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article: Bangalore is ___ ideal place for one's education.
explanation:
The article depends on the SOUND of the next word: 'ideal' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an ideal place'.
Memory hook: an before vowel SOUNDS (an ideal, an hour), a before consonant SOUNDS (a university, a one-way).

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article: Kobe Bryant is ___ basketball player.
explanation:
Singular countable noun, one member of a group (one of many basketball players) -> indefinite article; 'basketball' starts with a consonant sound -> 'a'.
Memory hook: 'a' = one of many; 'the' = the only / already known one.
note: Kobe Bryant died in January 2020; 'was' would be more accurate, but the article tested is unaffected.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article: Tennis is ___ very interesting game.
explanation:
The article agrees with the sound of the word immediately after it -- 'very' (consonant sound) -> 'a very interesting game', even though 'interesting' starts with a vowel.
Memory hook: look at the NEXT word only: a very interesting, an interesting.

q: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article: My uncle's car can do over 200 kilometres ___ hour.
explanation:
Both 'per hour' and 'an hour' mean 'in each hour'. Since this set tests articles, the intended answer is 'an' (vowel sound: 'hour' has a silent h). 'An' used distributively = per (Rs. 50 a kilo, 200 km an hour).
Memory hook: silent h -> an hour, an honest man, an heir.
note: Option a 'Per' is also grammatically correct (200 kilometres per hour). Chosen 'An' because the section heading is 'articles'; an official key could have 'Per'. Treat as ambiguous.

q: Identify the correct sentence.
options: He went to work despite of his illness
He went to work despite his illness
He went to worked despite his illness
explanation:
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. Use 'despite X' or 'in spite of X'. Also 'to' + base verb ('to work', not 'to worked').
Memory hook: 'in spite OF' has three words, 'despite' stands alone -- never 'despite of'.

q: Identify the correct sentence.
options: Raju, who he is my best friend, is a writer.
Raju, who my best friend is, is a writer.
Raju, who is my best friend, is a writer
explanation:
In a relative clause, 'who' itself is the subject, so no extra pronoun ('he') is added, and normal subject-verb order follows: who is my best friend.
Memory hook: 'who' replaces 'he' -- never use both.

q: Identify the correct sentence.
options: No matter what that I do, I can't make her happy
No matter what I do, I can't make her happy
No matter what I did, I can't make her happy
explanation:
'No matter what' is followed directly by a clause (no 'that'), and tenses must agree: present 'do' with present 'can't'. Option c mixes past 'did' with present 'can't'.
Memory hook: no matter what + subject + verb, same tense on both sides.

q: Identify the correct sentence.
options: She is busy at work and won't be home before 10.30
She is busy at the work and won't be home before 10.30.
She is busy at work and won't been home before 10.30
explanation:
'At work' is a fixed phrase with no article (like at home, at school, in bed). After modal 'won't' (will not), use the base form 'be', not 'been'.
Memory hook: modal + base verb: will be, won't be, can go.

q: Identify the correct sentence.
options: I have decided to quit my job a month ago
I had decided to quit my job a week ago
I have decided to quit my job a week ago.
explanation:
Present perfect ('have decided') cannot be used with a finished past-time expression like 'ago', 'yesterday', 'last week'. So a and c are wrong. Option b is the only acceptable choice here (the ideal sentence would be simple past: 'I decided to quit my job a week ago').
Memory hook: 'ago' is a past-tense word -- never with have/has.
note: Option b (past perfect + 'ago') is only acceptable relative to a later past event; the fully natural form is simple past. b is the intended answer by elimination.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word: Lavish
explanation:
Lavish = rich, luxurious, extravagant. Opulent = displaying great wealth/luxury. Scarce and deficient are opposites.
Memory hook: opulent -> 'opulence' of a palace = lavish.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word: Savage
explanation:
Savage = fierce, wild, untamed. Civilized is the antonym (trap).
Memory hook: savage beasts are wild beasts.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word: Timid
explanation:
Timid = shy, lacking courage. Meek = quiet, gentle, submissive. Bold is the antonym (trap).
Memory hook: 'timid as a mouse, meek as a lamb'.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word: Yoke
explanation:
A yoke is the wooden bar fastened over the necks of oxen; figuratively it means a heavy burden or oppression ('the yoke of colonial rule').
Memory hook: the oxen carry the yoke -> a burden on the shoulders. (Don't confuse with 'yolk' of an egg.)

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to the given word: Authentic
explanation:
Authentic = genuine, reliable, trustworthy. Fictitious (false, invented) is the antonym.
Memory hook: an authentic document comes from the 'author' himself -> genuine and trustworthy.

q: 'Checkpoint Tipline' which was in news is
options: Electronic toll collection on Toll plazas on National Highways
E-filing of Income tax by an individual
Platform launched by WhatsApp to address the issue of fake news during Lok Sabha elections
Resolving border issues between neighbouring countries
explanation:
Checkpoint Tipline was launched by WhatsApp (with Proto, an Indian media-skilling startup) in April 2019 so users could send suspicious messages for verification and to study misinformation during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections.
Memory hook: 'Tipline' = users send tips to WhatsApp to check fake news.

q: Mount Agung which witnessed volcanic eruption is located in
explanation:
Mount Agung is an active stratovolcano and the highest point on Bali, Indonesia; it erupted in 2017-2019.
Memory hook: Agung -> Bali's 'Gunung Agung' (gunung = mountain in Indonesian).

q: 'Param Shivay' is a
options: A device to predict weather in a particular region
explanation:
PARAM Shivay (833 TF) is the first supercomputer built indigenously under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), installed at IIT (BHU), Varanasi, inaugurated February 2019. Built by C-DAC.
Memory hook: 'Shivay' -> Lord Shiva -> Varanasi (Kashi) -> IIT BHU. All C-DAC 'PARAM' machines are supercomputers.
note: Topic tagged science-physics for want of a science-tech slug; it is a science & technology current-affairs item.

q: 'Lord Howe Island' which is a UNESCO world heritage site is located near
explanation:
Lord Howe Island Group is in the Tasman Sea, part of New South Wales, Australia; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982.
Memory hook: 'Lord Howe' was a British admiral -> British-named islands off Australia.

q: 'Garia Puja' is a puja done by the tribes of
explanation:
Garia Puja is a major festival of the Tripuri (and Reang) tribes of Tripura, held in April, worshipping Baba Garia for prosperity. It is a state holiday in Tripura.
Memory hook: GARIA -> 'Tri-GARIA-pura' -- Garia belongs to Tripura.

q: India is in the process of procuring the Spike-LR Anti Tank Missiles from
explanation:
Spike is a family of fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missiles made by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, Israel. India bought Spike-LR missiles (2019-2020 emergency procurement).
Memory hook: Spike, Barak, Heron, Python -- Israeli weapons.

q: Global Talent competitiveness Index has been released by
options: United Nations conference on Trade and development
explanation:
The Global Talent Competitiveness Index (GTCI) is published by INSEAD (French business school, Fontainebleau), with partners like the Portulans Institute/Adecco. Switzerland usually ranks 1st.
Memory hook: Talent -> Business school (INSEAD) trains talent.

q: National Science Day is observed on
explanation:
National Science Day (28 February) marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 (Nobel Prize in Physics, 1930).
Memory hook: 28 Feb 1928 -- '28' twice: Raman's day.

q: Who fixes REPO rate in India ?
explanation:
The Repo rate (rate at which RBI lends short-term to commercial banks) is fixed by the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (6 members, chaired by the RBI Governor), under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act.
Memory hook: Repo = RBI lends; Reverse repo = RBI borrows.

q: The book 'Gokhale, My Political Guru' was written by
explanation:
Mahatma Gandhi regarded Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political guru and wrote 'Gokhale: My Political Guru' (Navajivan, 1955 compilation).
Memory hook: Gandhi's political guru = Gokhale (both G); Gokhale's guru = M.G. Ranade.

q: Bodo and Dogri were added in the 8th schedule of the Constitution of India by the following amendment -
explanation:
The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added four languages -- Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali -- raising the Eighth Schedule to 22 languages. (21st Amendment 1967: Sindhi; 71st Amendment 1992: Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali.)
Memory hook: 'BDMS' -- Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali -> 92nd (2003).

q: The largest proven oil reserve of the world lies in
explanation:
Venezuela has the world's largest proven crude oil reserves (about 300 billion barrels, mostly heavy oil of the Orinoco Belt), ahead of Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia is the largest exporter, not the largest reserve holder.
Memory hook: reserves = Venezuela; exports = Saudi.

q: Which of the following statement is wrong?
options: Fundamental rights cannot be suspended during a national emergency
explanation:
Fundamental Rights (Part III) are justiciable/enforceable in courts (Art. 32 and 226), so 'non-enforceable' is wrong -- non-enforceability is a feature of the Directive Principles (Part IV, Art. 37). They are not absolute (reasonable restrictions apply).
Memory hook: FRs = enforceable (justiciable); DPSPs = non-justiciable.
note: Statement d is ALSO wrong: during a National Emergency, Art. 358 suspends Art. 19 automatically and Art. 359 lets the President suspend enforcement of other FRs (except Arts. 20 and 21, after the 44th Amendment). The question therefore has two wrong statements; b is the most likely intended key because it directly contradicts c.

q: Who among the following was responsible for the founding of Anglo-Muhammadan Oriental College ?
explanation:
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh in 1875; it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920. He led the Aligarh Movement.
Memory hook: Sir Syed -> Aligarh -> AMU.
note: The question names it 'Anglo-Muhammadan Oriental College'; the correct name is Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College.

q: India's first honey testing laboratory has been set up in which of the following states ?
explanation:
India's first (NABL-accredited) honey testing laboratory was set up by NDDB at Anand, Gujarat, inaugurated by Agriculture Minister Narendra Singh Tomar on 24 July 2020 under the National Beekeeping and Honey Mission.
Memory hook: Anand = 'Milk capital' (Amul, NDDB) -> NDDB now tests honey too: milk and honey in Gujarat.

q: The 'Bold Kurukshetra 2019' is a joint military exercise between
explanation:
Bold Kurukshetra is the India-Singapore bilateral armoured/mechanised army exercise; the 2019 (12th) edition was held at Babina, Jhansi (April 2019).
Memory hook: 'Bold' S-ingapore; other pairs -- Surya Kiran (Nepal), Garuda Shakti (Indonesia), AUSTRAHIND (Australia).

q: In which country of the world the largest Buddhist temple is located ?
explanation:
Borobudur, in Central Java, Indonesia (9th century, Sailendra dynasty), is the world's largest Buddhist temple and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Memory hook: BOROBudur = the BIGGEST (B-B).

q: Which of the following rights was considered by Dr. Ambedkar as the 'Heart and Soul' of the Indian Constitution ?
explanation:
Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it', since it makes all other FRs enforceable through writs in the Supreme Court.
Memory hook: Art. 32 = the right that protects all other rights -> heart and soul.

q: Who is known as 'Lauh Purush' of India ?
explanation:
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is the 'Iron Man of India' (Lauh Purush) for integrating about 560 princely states. Statue of Unity (Gujarat) honours him.
Memory hook: Lauh = iron (lohā) -> Iron Man -> Patel.

q: National Unity Day is celebrated on
explanation:
National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, since 2014.
Memory hook: Iron Man (Q69) -> his birthday 31 Oct = Unity Day.

q: Who among the following is the author of the book 'The Audacity of Hope' ?
explanation:
'The Audacity of Hope' (2006) was written by Barack Obama. His other books: 'Dreams from My Father' (1995), 'A Promised Land' (2020).
Memory hook: Obama's 2008 slogan was 'Hope' -> Audacity of Hope.

q: Where is the city of Yangon ?
explanation:
Yangon (formerly Rangoon) is Myanmar's largest city and former capital; the capital moved to Naypyidaw in 2005-06.
Memory hook: Rangoon -> Yangon; Burma -> Myanmar (both renamed 1989).

q: Who gave the first evidence of the Big-Bang theory ?
explanation:
Edwin Hubble (1929) showed galaxies are receding with speed proportional to distance (Hubble's law / redshift) -- the first observational evidence of an expanding universe, which underpins the Big Bang theory. (Theory proposed by Georges Lemaitre; CMB discovered by Penzias & Wilson in 1965.)
Memory hook: Hubble saw the universe 'bubble' outwards.
note: Strictly, the Big Bang was proposed after/alongside Hubble's discovery; Hubble's expansion is the standard 'first evidence' answer in GK books.

q: The Olympic Flame symbolises
options: Unity among various nations of the world
Continuity between the ancient and the modern games
Sports as a means of securing harmony among nations
explanation:
The Olympic flame, lit at Olympia (Greece) by the sun's rays and relayed to the host city, symbolises the continuity/link between the ancient Greek Games and the modern Olympics. (The five rings symbolise unity of the five continents; the motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' = Faster, Higher, Stronger.)
Memory hook: flame lit in ancient Olympia, carried to the modern host -> ancient-to-modern continuity.

q: Attorney General of India is appointed by
explanation:
Article 76: the Attorney General (highest law officer) is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President; must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.
Memory hook: Art. 76 AG; Art. 165 Advocate General (state, appointed by Governor).

q: What is the motto of the 2020 Summer Olympic which was held in Tokyo during Covid-19 pandemic ?
explanation:
Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021) motto: 'United by Emotion'. 'One World, One Dream' was Beijing 2008; 'Live your passion' was Rio 2016.
Memory hook: the pandemic kept fans apart, but athletes were United by Emotion.

q: In the context of Planning in India, when was NITI Aayog established ?
explanation:
NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission (1950) by a Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015. The PM is its ex-officio Chairperson.
Memory hook: New Year 2015 -> New institution (NITI).

q: Who among the following climbed the Mount Everest for the 25th time in May 2021 ?
explanation:
Kami Rita Sherpa (Nepal) made his record 25th Everest summit on 7 May 2021. Apa Sherpa and Phurba Tashi held the earlier record of 21 ascents.
Memory hook: KAMI Rita keeps COMING back to Everest.
note: As of the 2022 exam: 25 (2021), 26 (May 2022). As of Sept 2026: 32 ascents, the latest on 17 May 2026 (31st on 27 May 2025).

q: Mother Teresa was born in
explanation:
Mother Teresa (Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu) was born on 26 August 1910 in Skopje, then in the Ottoman Empire, now the capital of North Macedonia. Albanian by ethnicity; founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata (1950); Nobel Peace Prize 1979; canonised as St. Teresa of Calcutta in 2016.
Memory hook: Skopje -> Macedonia.
note: Macedonia was renamed North Macedonia in February 2019.

q: 'Kundankulam Project' is located in which state ?
explanation:
Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (built with Russian collaboration, VVER reactors) is in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu -- India's largest nuclear power station.
Memory hook: Kudankulam -> near Kanyakumari tip -> Tamil Nadu.
note: Printed as 'Kundankulam'; the correct spelling is Kudankulam.

q: Which of the following Schedules to the Constitution of India relates to languages ?
explanation:
The Eighth Schedule lists the 22 official languages. 7th = Union/State/Concurrent lists; 9th = laws protected from judicial review (1st Amendment); 10th = anti-defection (52nd Amendment).
Memory hook: 8th = 22 languages (the 92nd Amendment made it 22).

q: Who wrote "Saare jahan se achha Hindustan humara" ?
explanation:
Muhammad Iqbal wrote 'Tarana-e-Hind' (Saare Jahan Se Achha) in 1904 in Urdu. Bankim Chandra wrote Vande Mataram (Anandamath); Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana.
Memory hook: Iqbal also appears in Q64's options -- poet of the East.

q: Who authored the book 'India from Midnight to Millennium' ?
explanation:
'India: From Midnight to the Millennium' (1997) is by Shashi Tharoor, written for 50 years of Independence. Other Tharoor books: 'An Era of Darkness', 'The Great Indian Novel', 'Why I Am a Hindu'.
Memory hook: 'Midnight' (15 Aug 1947) -> Tharoor.

q: Who is the Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha ?
explanation:
Article 64 and Article 89: the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.
Memory hook: Vice-President = Upper house (both 'V'/'U' up).

q: Which of the following is the first state to have been formed on the liguistic basis ?
explanation:
Andhra State was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953 for Telugu speakers, after Potti Sriramulu's death following a fast-unto-death. It became Andhra Pradesh in 1956 (States Reorganisation Act).
Memory hook: Potti Sriramulu -> first linguistic state -> Andhra.
note: 'liguistic' is a print typo for 'linguistic'. Strictly, the first was 'Andhra State' (1953), renamed Andhra Pradesh in 1956.

q: Which of the following Articles of Indian Constitution deal with 'Right to Religion' ?
explanation:
FR blocks: 14-18 Equality; 19-22 Freedom; 23-24 Against exploitation; 25-28 Freedom of Religion; 29-30 Cultural & educational; 32 Constitutional remedies.
Memory hook: 'E-F-E-R-C-C' -> 14, 19, 23, 25, 29, 32.

q: The largest population of Scheduled Tribes in India is in the state of (as per 2011 census)
explanation:
Census 2011: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population (about 1.53 crore, 14.7% of India's STs), followed by Maharashtra and Odisha. By percentage, Mizoram (94.4%) and Lakshadweep lead; Meghalaya is 86.1% ST.
Memory hook: MP = Most People (tribal, in absolute numbers).

q: What is the full form of RAM in a computer?
explanation:
RAM = Random Access Memory -- volatile primary memory that loses data when power is off. ROM = Read Only Memory (non-volatile).
Memory hook: RAM forgets when you switch off; ROM remembers.

q: 'Eco mark' is given to the Indian products that are
explanation:
Ecomark (launched 1991 by the Environment Ministry; certification then run through the Bureau of Indian Standards) certifies products as environment-friendly. Its logo is an earthen pot (matka). Compare: Agmark = agricultural products; ISI = industrial products; FPO = fruit products.
Memory hook: ECO = ecology = environment.
note: Current status (as of Sept 2026): the Ecomark Rules, 2024 (notified 26 Sept 2024) replaced the 1991 scheme; the Central Pollution Control Board is now the implementing authority, working with BIS. The answer (environment-friendly) is unchanged.

q: In which date the prestigious Nobel Prize is awarded (i.e. the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death) ?
explanation:
Nobel Prizes are presented on 10 December, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death (1896) -- in Stockholm, except the Peace Prize in Oslo.
Memory hook: 10 December is also Human Rights Day.

q: 'Habeas Corpus' writ is associated with
options: Quashing the order of Un-administrative authority
An order of freedom of speech
explanation:
Habeas Corpus ('you may have the body') orders a detaining authority to produce the detained person before the court, to test whether the detention is lawful. Other writs: Mandamus (we command), Prohibition, Certiorari (to be certified -- quashes orders), Quo Warranto (by what authority).
Memory hook: 'Corpus' = body -> bring the body to court.

q: On a sudden cardiac arrest, which of the following is advised as a first step to revive the functioning of human heart ?
explanation:
In cardiac arrest, the first priority in CPR is chest compressions (external cardiac massage) to keep blood flowing to the brain. Current guidelines use C-A-B (Compressions first, then Airway, Breathing).
Memory hook: 'Push hard, push fast' -- compressions come first.

q: Which of the following is needed by a person suffering from diabetes ?
explanation:
Diabetes mellitus results from lack of or resistance to insulin, the hormone of the beta cells in the Islets of Langerhans (pancreas) that lowers blood sugar. The other options are antibiotics (for bacterial infections).
Memory hook: Insulin lets sugar go IN to cells.

q: Pressure cooker cooks rice faster because
options: It always lets the steam escape
High pressure crushes the hard covering of rice grains
It does not let the heat energy escape easily
High pressure raises the boiling point of water
explanation:
Boiling point rises with pressure. Inside a pressure cooker (about 2 atm) water boils at about 120 degrees C instead of 100 degrees C, so food cooks faster. Conversely, at high altitudes, low pressure lowers the boiling point, so cooking is slower.
Memory hook: more pressure -> hotter boiling water -> faster cooking.

q: The clear sky looks blue because of
explanation:
Rayleigh scattering: air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths (blue) much more than longer ones (red), since scattering is proportional to 1/wavelength^4. The same explains red sunsets.
Memory hook: Sky Scatters -- S-S.

q: The drug quinine is used in the treatment of
explanation:
Quinine, from the bark of the cinchona tree, is an antimalarial drug. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito.
Memory hook: Cinchona -> Quinine -> Kills malaria.

q: The words of which poem are inscribed on the entrance to the players tunnel at Wimbledon?
options: The Lesson for Today (by Robert Frost)
explanation:
Above the players' entrance to Centre Court at Wimbledon are lines from Rudyard Kipling's 'If': 'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster / And treat those two impostors just the same'.
Memory hook: win or lose at Wimbledon -- IF you treat both the same.

q: Which of the following International organization releases the Global Environment outlook Report ?
options: International Union for Conservation of Nature
explanation:
The Global Environment Outlook (GEO) is UNEP's flagship assessment (GEO-6 in 2019; GEO-7 in 2025). IUCN publishes the Red List; WWF publishes the Living Planet Report; FAO publishes State of the World's Forests.
Memory hook: GEO = Global Environment Outlook = UN Environment Programme.
note: GEO-7 was released in December 2025 (latest edition as of Sept 2026).

q: What is 'Staphylococcus epidermidis' ?
options: A flowering plant found in upper Himalayas
A virus found on International space station
A bacteria found on human skin
explanation:
Staphylococcus epidermidis is a Gram-positive bacterium that is a normal part of the human skin flora (epidermis). Research (2018) showed a strain producing a compound (6-HAP) that may protect against skin cancer.
Memory hook: 'epidermidis' -> epidermis = skin; 'coccus' = spherical bacterium.

q: The scheme 'Kishan Kalyan Pradhikaran' was launched to increase farm productivity and farmers income. Which of the following states has launched the scheme ?
explanation:
Haryana set up the Haryana Kisan Kalyan Pradhikaran (Haryana Kisan Kalyan Pradhikaran Act, 2018) to integrate schemes for farmers' welfare and doubling of farmers' income. (Haryana also runs Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana.)
Memory hook: HARyana = HARvest welfare authority.
